The SSRF guard.

Checks the RESOLVED address, not the hostname, and returns that address so
the caller can pin the connection to it. Checking the name and then letting
the HTTP client resolve again is the DNS-rebinding hole that this closes.

props.doc:
Turn what the no-code builder collected into a real command definition.

This is the function behind "Method / URL / Headers / Body / Output" in the
UI. What comes out is an ordinary command version, indistinguishable at the
engine from one an engineer wrote - which is the property that stops the
no-code path from being a second-class citizen.
props.name: build_definition

props.code:
method = str(form.get("method", "GET")).upper()
if method not in ("GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE", "HEAD"):
    raise ValueError("unsupported method")

mutating = method not in ("GET", "HEAD")
return {
    "key": form["key"],
    "name": form["name"],
    "category": form.get("category", "custom"),
    "kind": "http",
    "input_schema": form.get("input_schema", {"type": "object", "properties": {}}),
    "output_schema": form.get("output_schema", {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {"status": {"type": "integer"}, "body": {"type": "object"}},
    }),
    "implementation": {
        "method": method,
        "url": form["url"],
        "headers": form.get("headers", {}),
        "body": form.get("body"),
        "extract": form.get("extract", {}),
        "success_codes": form.get("success_codes", [200, 201, 202, 204]),
    },
    "auth": form.get("auth", []),
    "required_permissions": ["commands.execute"],
    "required_capabilities": ["net"],
    "timeout_ms": int(form.get("timeout_ms", 15000)),
    "risk_level": form.get("risk_level", "medium" if mutating else "low"),
    "effect": "mutating" if mutating else "read",
    "trust_level": "verified",
    "dry_run_example": form.get("dry_run_example", {"status": 200, "body": {}}) if mutating else None,
    "doc": form.get("doc", ""),
}

props.doc:
Substitute the integration settings into a template without encoding them.

The renderer percent-encodes everything it places in a URL, which is right
for an input - a hostname arriving from an alert must not be able to add a
path segment. It is wrong for the base URL itself: encoding the scheme and
the colon turns https://host into a path segment of whatever came before.
Settings are typed into an admin form and screened against the egress
allowlist afterwards, so they are substituted literally and the encoding
rule stays where the untrusted data is.
props.name: fill_settings

props.code:

for name, value in (config or {}).items():
    result = result.replace("{{ integration.config.%s }}" % name, str(value))
return result

props.doc:
Put the leased credential where this vendor expects it, and return the URL
to actually request.

Every product authenticates differently - a bearer token, a bare key in a
header nobody else uses, a key in the query string, two headers that have
to agree, an OAuth exchange against a tenant-specific endpoint. The
connector manifest says which; nothing here knows a vendor by name, so a
new one is a manifest and not a patch.
props.name: apply_auth

props.code:
from soar.playbooks.template import encode_for

import base64
import urllib.parse

if not scheme:
    return url

kind = scheme.get("kind")
roles = scheme.get("roles") or []

def secret(role):
    # encode_for reveals a secret for a header and masks it everywhere else,
    # so the one place that may see plaintext stays the one place that does.
    return encode_for(lease.get(role), "header")

if kind == "oauth2_client":
    headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer " + oauth_token(
        scheme, lease, context, allowlist, timeout_ms)
    return url

if kind == "session":
    # An appliance that has you sign in and then carry a cookie. Common
    # enough on things that were a web console before they were an API.
    headers.update(session_headers(scheme, lease, context, url, allowlist,
                                   timeout_ms))
    return url

if kind == "basic":
    if len(roles) < 2:
        raise ValueError("basic auth needs a user role and a secret role")
    pair = "%s:%s" % (secret(roles[0]), secret(roles[1]))
    headers["Authorization"] = "Basic " + base64.b64encode(
        pair.encode("utf-8")).decode("ascii")
    return url

if kind != "api_key":
    raise ValueError("unsupported auth kind %r" % kind)

# Some products want one key in two places, or two different keys in two
# headers that have to arrive together.
per_role = scheme.get("headers") or {}
if per_role:
    for role, header_name in per_role.items():
        prefix = (scheme.get("prefixes") or {}).get(role, "")
        headers[header_name] = prefix + secret(role)
    return url

if scheme.get("header"):
    headers[scheme["header"]] = scheme.get("prefix", "") + secret(roles[0])
    return url

if scheme.get("query"):
    # The key goes in the URL. It is appended here rather than through a
    # template because the renderer masks secrets in a URL on purpose, and
    # that rule is worth more than the convenience of writing it inline.
    parts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(url)
    query = urllib.parse.parse_qsl(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True)
    query.append((scheme["query"], secret(roles[0])))
    return urllib.parse.urlunsplit((
        parts.scheme, parts.netloc, parts.path,
        urllib.parse.urlencode(query), ""))

# No header, no query: the connector puts the key in the request body with
# a {{ credentials.<role> }} template, which is a legitimate place for it.
return url

Sign in, and return the headers that carry the session.

The shape is declared, not coded: which path to post to, what to send,
and whether the answer comes back as a cookie or as a value somewhere in
the response body. A product that hands back a session id in JSON and one
that sets a cookie are the same three lines of manifest apart, and neither
is a vendor branch in here.

props.doc:
Exchange a client id and secret for an access token, and keep it until it
is nearly expired.

The token endpoint is templated, because for Microsoft it contains the
tenant and there is one tenant per client. It is screened against the same
allowlist as the command itself: a manifest that can be pointed at an
arbitrary token endpoint is a credential exfiltration primitive.
props.name: oauth_token

props.code:
from soar.platform.runtime import services
from soar.playbooks.template import encode_for, render

import httpx
import json
import time

connection = context["integration"]["config"]
token_url = render(fill_settings(scheme["token_url"], connection),
                   context, position="url")

# The token endpoint lives on the same cloud as the API. A manifest that
# hard-codes the commercial one would send a EU tenant to sign in in the
# United States, where its client id does not exist.
configured = str(connection.get("base_url") or "").strip()
if configured:
    import urllib.parse as parse_url
    want = parse_url.urlsplit(configured)
    have = parse_url.urlsplit(token_url)
    same_product = (have.netloc.split(".")[-2:]
                    == want.netloc.split(".")[-2:])
    # Only when the token endpoint belongs to the product itself. An
    # identity provider on its own domain - login.microsoftonline.com for
    # every Microsoft product - stays where it is whatever the API host is.
    if want.netloc and have.netloc != want.netloc and same_product:
        token_url = parse_url.urlunsplit(
            (want.scheme or have.scheme, want.netloc, have.path,
             have.query, ""))
check_destination(token_url, allowlist)

roles = scheme.get("roles") or ["client_id", "client_secret"]
client_id = encode_for(lease.get(roles[0]), "header")
client_secret = encode_for(lease.get(roles[1]), "header")

# Cached in Redis, so every worker shares one exchange rather than each
# holding its own. CrowdStrike rate-limits token requests hard enough
# that one per command per process is the thing that breaks a
# containment at the worst moment.
key = "oauth:%s:%s" % (token_url, client_id)
if scheme.get("scope"):
    key += ":" + scheme["scope"]

shared = None
try:
    shared = services()["redis"]
except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - a test or a tool may have no services
    shared = None

if shared is not None:
    held = shared.get(key)
    if held:
        return held.decode("utf-8") if isinstance(held, bytes) else held
else:
    # No Redis in this process: fall back to one cache per process
    # rather than an exchange per call.
    cache = getattr(fetch_oauth_token, "cache", None)
    if cache is None:
        cache = {}
        fetch_oauth_token.cache = cache
    cached = cache.get(key)
    if cached and cached[1] > time.time():
        return cached[0]

form = {"grant_type": "client_credentials",
        "client_id": client_id, "client_secret": client_secret}
if scheme.get("scope"):
    form["scope"] = scheme["scope"]

with httpx.Client(timeout=timeout_ms / 1000.0, follow_redirects=False) as client:
    response = client.post(token_url, data=form)
if response.status_code != 200:
    raise RuntimeError(json.dumps({
        "error_class": "AUTH",
        "status": response.status_code,
        "message": "token endpoint refused the client credentials",
    }))

payload = response.json()
token = payload.get("access_token")
if not token:
    raise RuntimeError(json.dumps({
        "error_class": "AUTH", "status": 200,
        "message": "token endpoint returned no access_token",
    }))

# Sixty seconds of headroom, so a token cannot expire between the check and
# the request it was fetched for.
ttl = max(int(payload.get("expires_in", 1800)) - 60, 30)
if shared is not None:
    shared.setex(key, ttl, token)
else:
    fetch_oauth_token.cache[key] = (token, time.time() + ttl)
return token
